# onetsolutions_instance_backup (Resource)

Takes an on-demand backup of an instance's disks, kept for its retention period.

~> **Billing.** Backups need the instance's **backup option**, a paid add-on billed with the
instance: order it with the instance in `addon_ids`, or add it in the console. The backups
themselves are not billed one by one. Without the option, the plan fails.

!> **Destroying does not delete the backup.** A backup cannot be deleted: `terraform destroy`, or a
change that replaces this resource, only removes it from the state, with a warning in the plan and
after the apply. The backup remains available, for restores and in `onetsolutions_instance_backups`,
until it expires at `expires_at`, `retention_days` after it was taken.

Creating the resource requests the backup and waits until it is complete, up to the `create`
timeout (3 hours by default); a backup requested while another operation runs on the instance waits
for it to end. A backup cannot be changed: a new `name`, `instance_id` or `retention_days` takes a
new backup, and the previous one remains.

A name is unique on the instance for as long as its backup exists, failed and expired ones
included, so a new backup always needs a new name: the plan fails on a name already taken. A
backup that failed stays in the state, tainted, with status `failed`; give it a new name to take
another.

Once its retention has passed, the backup stays in the state with status `deleted`, so the
configuration does not take a new one under the same name. When the instance is cancelled or
terminated, the next refresh removes the resource from the state.

Restore a backup with the `onetsolutions_instance_backup_restore` action.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onetsolutions_instance_backup" "before_upgrade" {
  instance_id    = onetsolutions_instance.web.id
  name           = "before-php-8-4-upgrade"
  retention_days = 7

  timeouts {
    create = "4h"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `instance_id` (String) The UUID of the instance to back up; it must have the backup option. Changing it takes a new backup.
- `name` (String) The name of the backup, at most 255 characters, unique on the instance among all its backups, expired ones included. Changing it takes a new backup.

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) The organization the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `organization_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `project_id` (String) The project the object belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `project_id` when the object is created; changing it explicitly recreates the object.
- `retention_days` (Number) How many days the backup is kept, from 1 to 7. Defaults to 7. Changing it takes a new backup, which needs a new `name`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `backup_type` (String) `manual` for an on-demand backup, `scheduled` for one taken by the backup schedule.
- `created` (String) When the backup was requested (RFC 3339).
- `expires_at` (String) When the backup expires and is deleted (RFC 3339).
- `id` (String) The UUID of the backup.
- `size_gb` (String) The size of the backup in GB, a decimal such as `3.20`; null until it is complete.
- `status` (String) The status of the backup: `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `deleted` once its retention has passed.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the creation, as a duration such as "30s" or "2h45m". Defaults to `3h`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = onetsolutions_instance_backup.before_upgrade
  id = "3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <organization_id>/<project_id>/<instance_id>/<backup_id>, or <instance_id>/<backup_id> when the provider sets organization_id and project_id.
terraform import onetsolutions_instance_backup.before_upgrade 3f2a9c1e-5b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b/8b1d4e2f-6c3a-4f9e-8d7b-2a1c0e9f8d7c/9a0b1c2d-3e4f-4a5b-8c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d/5e6f7a8b-9c0d-4e1f-8a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b
```
